verdicts.reason: A keeps the three plan cards readable and in their original Monthly/Yearly/Family order, and reads left to right through to the CTA. But it is badly cramped: the cards nearly touch the top edge, the legal line is jammed along the bottom, the price numerals compete with a fairly small headline, and the subhead wraps awkwardly. B gives the headline strong hierarchy, but it shrinks the plan cards into tiny chips whose labels and 'per month' text can't be read. It also reorders them to 6/80/48, which breaks the sequence. The 48 card butts against the CTA, and the subhead and legal copy are crammed into a ragged block against the right edge, so the core pricing message is lost.
